purpose: Resolve the post-carrier-battle amphibious timing and the first day of the Branch Kwajalein/Roi-Namur landings, preserving Tarawa-derived US amphibious improvements and the stronger-but-degrading Japanese warning network.

why_not_5Feb: 3-Feb carrier exchange consumes a suppression/air-superiority day and temporarily interrupts Intrepid while removing Cabot.
Marshall local aviation remains nonzero and water-air/submarine reconnaissance continues.
An extra day permits old-battleship/CVE/TF57 suppression, channel-islet work and redistribution after LST-224 loss.
why_not_later: Intrepid is back near normal by 4-Feb; ten US fast decks remain.
Assault troops and shipping are already on station; waiting longer increases submarine/night-air exposure.
US fire-support and CVE forces remain largely intact and can compensate for the one lost LST.

prelanding_4_5Feb.Majuro: Occupied by the small US Majuro group on 4-Feb centered with no organized resistance; anchorage immediately useful for security/logistics, full base development still future.
prelanding_4_5Feb.air_and_naval_suppression: 4-5 Feb use TF58, TF57/Gilberts, six CVE close-support groups and old battleships/cruisers to continue Taroa/Roi/Kwajalein/Wotje suppression and detailed beach/fire-plan preparation. 3-Feb carrier battle prevents a perfectly uninterrupted historical-style schedule but does not remove overwhelming US local firepower.
prelanding_4_5Feb.Japanese_air_before_main_landing: Marshall serviceable combat aircraft fall from ~47 at 3-Feb 15:30 to about 24-30 at 6-Feb dawn centered ~27; only about 10-13 are serviceable fighters and 4-6 attack aircraft. Water-air/recon retains a few useful aircraft, so warning survives longer than runway-based strike strength.
prelanding_4_5Feb.Kinsei_forward_order: The late-Jan 6-8 Kinsei forward-order is stopped/retained at Truk/Ponape staging after the 2-3 Feb suppression picture; no late magical reinforcement into Taroa/Roi is credited.

landing_execution.preliminary_islets: 5-Feb late/6-Feb pre-dawn: channel/flanking islets are seized to open lagoon approaches and establish artillery/observation; resistance is light-to-moderate and cannot deny the passes.
landing_execution.Roi_Namur: 4th Marine Division main assault 6-Feb morning after heavy naval/air preparation. Roi beachhead and much of the airfield are secured by evening; organized resistance remains on/around Namur and debris/strongpoints. The alerted defenders inflict more local casualties than a completely surprised garrison but cannot form a coherent beach denial system under the bombardment.
landing_execution.Kwajalein: 7th Infantry Division main assault 6-Feb morning. LVT/LVT(A), artillery from flanking islets, destroyer/old-battleship gunfire and CVE support put the first waves ashore successfully. The loss of one tractor-unit LST reduces equipment/unloading margin but does not strand a regiment. By evening a secure western beachhead and meaningful inland advance are established; island not yet declared secure.
landing_execution.air_interference: Remaining Japanese aircraft mount scattered interception/recon/harassment, not a coordinated mass strike. US CAP and repeated runway/lagoon-node suppression prevent them from disrupting the landing timetable.

centered_first_day_costs.US_ground_and_landing_force: Not a full-campaign total. 6-Feb landing/ashore combat centered roughly 430-620 killed+wounded across northern and southern sectors, excluding the LST-224 submarine casualties; higher than the extremely smooth historical first landing hours but far below Tarawa-level failure.
centered_first_day_costs.US_submarine_interdiction: LST-224 loss adds about 70-110 killed/missing/wounded and material/vehicle loss before D-Day.
centered_first_day_costs.Japan: Several thousand garrison troops remain fighting at 18:00; no centered surrender/collapse on the first main-assault day. Air component is nearly combat-exhausted but not literally zero.

state_at_1800.US: Both main beachheads secure enough to sustain unloading. Roi largely overrun; Namur and Kwajalein continue. D-Day succeeds operationally.
state_at_1800.Japan: Kwajalein/Roi-Namur cannot be reinforced at scale. Remaining submarines and water-air give warning/reporting but no operational mechanism exists to eject the landing force.
state_at_1800.next: Resolve 7-9 Feb ground reduction, remaining submarine attrition/withdrawal and post-capture airfield/logistics activation; then re-evaluate Eniwetok/Truk timing with Cabot out and Japanese carrier-air cadre debt.

historical_sanity_anchors: Historical Flintlock used about 54,000 assault troops and nearly 300 amphibious/support ships, with 4th Marine Division at Roi-Namur and 7th Infantry Division at Kwajalein.
Historical US amphibious improvements after Tarawa included LVT(A), improved LVT-2 and gun/rocket LCIs; Branch retains these lessons.
Historical Kwajalein was decided by overwhelming naval gunfire/air support and division-scale amphibious lift; Branch Japanese warning changes the cost and timing, not this force ratio.
